config.title: Form Library from Scratch

intro.title: Form Library from Scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form library from scratch to manage form state and validation in a React application. You will learn the core concept of controlled components, where form inputs are directly tied to React state. The main technologies involved are React hooks like useState and useReducer, along with TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable custom hook that can handle form values, track changes, and submit data.
intro.usecase: Building custom form libraries is essential in enterprise applications where complex validation, dynamic field generation, and consistent UX patterns are required. You'll see this pattern in admin dashboards like Shopify's store configuration, where merchants set up shipping rules with interdependent form fields. Customer portals like banking apps use similar libraries for multi-step loan applications with real-time validation. Even SaaS platforms like HubSpot implement custom form solutions for their marketing automation workflows, where forms adapt based on user selections and business rules.

objectives: Define TypeScript interfaces to structure form state with fields, values, and validation errors
Implement a useForm custom hook to manage form state and lifecycle
Apply useState hooks to store and update form field values dynamically
Utilize event handlers to capture and process user input from form elements
Construct validation functions to check field values against defined rules
Execute conditional rendering to display validation error messages when rules are violated
Use controlled components to bind form inputs to React state values
Implement form submission handlers to process validated data
Apply TypeScript generics to create reusable form components with type safety
Return structured form data with validation status from the custom hook
Control form reset functionality to clear all fields and errors
Modify form state to track dirty/pristine status for individual fields

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The code should include an import statement that imports React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check that you're using the correct import syntax with curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main Form component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Form that accepts children as props and returns a form element. Use TypeScript syntax with proper typing for the props.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes children as props and returns a <form> element wrapping those children.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Form component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Form component is defined with proper TypeScript typing that accepts children and returns a form element.
successCriteria: Component named Form is defined
Accepts children prop with React.ReactNode type
Returns a <form> element wrapping children
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Form component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Form component accepts children as props with the correct type and returns a <form> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Form component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a component named Form that accepts children and returns a form element.

steps.title: Define the FormField interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named FormField with three required properties: name (string), label (string), and initialValue (string). Place this interface definition above your Form component.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Each property should have a type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a FormField interface with the correct property types that can be used later to type form field configurations.
successCriteria: The code must include an interface named FormField with exactly three properties: name (string), label (string), and initialValue (string).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the FormField interface with the correct properties and types. This interface will help ensure type safety when working with form fields.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your FormField interface has all three required properties with the correct TypeScript types: name (string), label (string), and initialValue (string).
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormField interface is not correctly defined. Make sure you're using the 'interface' keyword, the correct interface name, and all three properties with their proper TypeScript types.

steps.title: Create the useForm hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook named useForm that accepts an array of FormField objects as its parameter. The hook should return an object with a fields property containing the form fields.
steps.hint: Define a function called useForm that takes a fields parameter typed as FormField[]. Return an object with a fields property set to the parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook named useForm is created that accepts FormField[] and returns { fields: FormField[] }.
successCriteria: Function named useForm
Parameter typed as FormField[]
Returns object with fields property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useForm hook that accepts form fields and returns them in an object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your hook is named useForm, accepts a FormField[] parameter, and returns an object with a fields property containing those fields.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't quite right. Remember to create a function called useForm that takes FormField[] and returns { fields: FormField[] }.

steps.title: Initialize form state in useForm
steps.instruction: Inside the useForm hook, use useState to create a formValues state object that will store the form data. Initialize it as an empty object {}.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty object as the initial value. Remember to specify the type parameter for useState to ensure type safety.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with an object
const [formValues, setFormValues] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook now has a formValues state variable initialized as an empty object, ready to store form field values.
successCriteria: The useForm hook contains a useState call that initializes formValues as an empty object with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the formValues state with an empty object. This will serve as the storage for all form field values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've properly initialized the state with an empty object and included the appropriate TypeScript type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useForm hook doesn't yet have the formValues state initialized. Make sure to use useState with an empty object as the initial value.

steps.title: Create the handleChange function
steps.instruction: Inside the useForm function, create a function named handleChange that takes an event parameter and updates the formValues state.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts a React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement> parameter and uses the setFormValues function to update the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook now contains a handleChange function that will be used to update form values when inputs change.
successCriteria: The useForm function should contain a handleChange function that accepts an event parameter and uses setFormValues to update state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleChange function. This function will handle input changes in our form.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function named handleChange that accepts an event parameter and uses setFormValues to update the formValues state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function isn't properly defined. You need to create a function inside useForm that will handle input changes.

steps.title: Create the handleSubmit function
steps.instruction: Inside the useForm hook, create a function named handleSubmit that takes an event parameter of type React.FormEvent, prevents the default form submission, and logs the current formValues to the console.
steps.hint: Define the function with the correct parameter type and use event.preventDefault() to stop the page from reloading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook now has a handleSubmit function that prevents default form submission and logs form values.
successCriteria: The handleSubmit function is defined inside useForm, accepts a React.FormEvent parameter, calls event.preventDefault(), and logs formValues to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleSubmit function that will handle form submissions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleSubmit function: 1) Accepts a React.FormEvent parameter, 2) Calls event.preventDefault(), and 3) Logs formValues to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function wasn't created correctly. Remember to define it inside useForm with the proper parameter type and prevent default form submission.

steps.title: Return values from useForm hook
steps.instruction: At the end of the useForm function, return an object containing formValues, handleChange, and handleSubmit.
steps.hint: Add a return statement at the end of the useForm function that returns an object with those three properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook now returns an object containing formValues, handleChange, and handleSubmit, making these values available to components that use the hook.
successCriteria: The useForm function should end with a return statement that returns an object with properties formValues, handleChange, and handleSubmit.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the form state and handlers from your custom hook. This makes them available to any component that calls useForm().
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning an object with all three required properties: formValues, handleChange, and handleSubmit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useForm hook needs to return an object containing formValues, handleChange, and handleSubmit. Check that you've added a return statement at the end of the function.

steps.title: Create the InputField component
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named InputField that accepts props: name (string), label (string), value (string), and onChange (function). The component should return JSX with a label and an input element.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called InputField. Use destructuring to get the props parameters. Return a JSX fragment or div containing a label element (with htmlFor set to name) and an input element (with name, value, and onChange attributes).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new InputField component that can be used to render form fields with labels and inputs.
successCriteria: Component named InputField is defined
Accepts name, label, value, and onChange as props
Returns JSX with a label and input element
Label uses htmlFor attribute
Input has name, value, and onChange attributes
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the InputField component. This reusable component will help render individual form fields with proper labels and inputs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but something is missing. Make sure your InputField component accepts all required props (name, label, value, onChange) and returns JSX with both a label and input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The InputField component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a component named InputField with the proper props and JSX structure.

steps.title: Implement the InputField JSX structure
steps.instruction: In the InputField component, return a JSX structure containing a div wrapper with a label element and an input element. The label should display the field's label prop, and the input should have its type and name attributes set from the props.
steps.hint:
The InputField component receives props (name, label, type). Return JSX like
.
steps.expectedOutcome: The InputField component now returns a structured JSX with a label and input, ready to be used in a form.
successCriteria: InputField returns JSX
JSX includes a div wrapper
JSX includes a label element with {label}
JSX includes an input element with type={type} and name={name}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the InputField JSX structure with proper labeling and input attributes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your InputField returns JSX with a div containing both a label (showing the label prop) and an input (with type and name from props).
steps.feedbackWrong: The InputField component should return JSX structure. Check that you're returning a div with a label and input element, using the props for their content and attributes.

steps.title: Create form configuration and use the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the Form component, create a formFields array with field configurations and call the useForm hook with it to get form state and handlers.
steps.hint: Define an array of objects that match the FormField interface, then call useForm(formFields) to get the returned values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form component will have a formFields array with field configurations and will call useForm to get form state and handlers.
successCriteria: The code should include: 1) A formFields array with at least one field object matching FormField interface, 2) A call to useForm(formFields) that destructures the returned values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the form configuration and connected it to your custom form hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a formFields array with field objects and called useForm with it to get the returned values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a formFields array with field configurations and call useForm with it inside the Form component.

steps.title: Build the form UI with InputField components
steps.instruction: In the Form component, map through the formFields array to render InputField components for each field, and add a submit button that calls handleSubmit when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the map method on formFields. For each field, return an InputField component with the appropriate props. Add a button element with type='submit' and onClick={handleSubmit}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form component will render a complete form with input fields for each item in formFields and a submit button that logs the form values when clicked.
successCriteria: Map through formFields array
Render InputField component for each field
Include key prop on each InputField
Add a submit button with onClick={handleSubmit}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully built the form UI by mapping through the formFields and rendering InputField components, and added a submit button wired to handleSubmit.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping through formFields, rendering InputField with the correct props (name, label, type), and adding a submit button that calls handleSubmit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form UI isn't complete. You need to map through formFields to render InputField components and add a submit button that triggers handleSubmit.
